# Root Native UI

> A component library for React Native that follows your design system. Material Design 3 is the default.

Root Native UI (`@rootnative`) is a React Native component library with a pluggable theme engine. Material Design 3 is the default design system. A custom design system goes through `BaseTheme`, `ThemeProvider`, and `defineTheme`.

## Packages

- `@rootnative/core`: the theme engine (`BaseTheme`, `ThemeProvider`, `defineTheme`, `useTheme`), the MD3 preset (`material`, light/dark themes), and the responsive breakpoint hooks
- `@rootnative/utils`: internal shared utilities: color helpers (`alphaColor`, `blendColor`), elevation styles, RTL support, the icon resolver. **Not published to npm.** It is bundled into `@rootnative/components`, and the CLI copies the needed files into your project on `rootnative add`. Don't tell users to install it.
- `@rootnative/components`: the UI components (AppBar, Avatar, Badge, BottomAppBar, BottomSheet, Button, ButtonGroup, Card, Checkbox, Chip, Dialog, Divider, FAB, Icon, IconButton, KeyboardAvoidingWrapper, Layout with Box / Row / Column / Grid / Container, List, LoadingIndicator, Menu, NavigationBar, NavigationDrawer, NavigationRail, Portal, Progress, Radio, SearchBar, SearchView, SideSheet, Skeleton, Slider, Snackbar, Switch, Tabs, TextField, Tooltip, Typography)
- `@rootnative/inertia`: the animation engine. A required peer of `core` and `components`. Every animation in the library routes through it, and it obeys the OS reduce-motion setting by default. Docs: https://rootnative.github.io/inertia/
- `@rootnative/icons`: icon-library adapters: `createLucideResolver`, `createPhosphorResolver`, `createVectorIconsResolver`, `withLegacyMdiFallback`. Lucide and Phosphor are optional peer deps. `createVectorIconsResolver` takes any `@react-native-vector-icons/*` set.
- `@rootnative/seo`: what a crawler reads from a web export: `defineSite` + `PageHead` for the head of each page, JSON-LD builders under `/schema`, `Heading` for the outline, `shellTags` for `+html.tsx`, and `writeSitemap` / `writeRobots` / `writeManifest` under `/node`. The core has no dependency. Docs: https://rootnative.github.io/ui/seo/why

## Quick start

### New project

```bash
npx rootnative create my-app
cd my-app
npx expo start
```

The `create` command makes a ready-to-run Expo project with `ThemeProvider` and example components set up. It asks for the project name, the display name, and the package manager.

### Existing project

```bash
pnpm add @rootnative/core @rootnative/components @rootnative/inertia react-native-safe-area-context react-native-svg react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets
```

Add `@react-native-vector-icons/material-design-icons` only when you use the default `mdiResolver` from `@rootnative/components/mdi`.

**Don't use `@expo/vector-icons`.** Expo is retiring it (https://expo.dev/blog/moving-away-from-expo-vector-icons). Use the `@react-native-vector-icons/*` package of the same icon family, and run `npx @react-native-vector-icons/codemod` on app code that imports the old package. Don't keep both installed: they register the same font, and the glyphs render as `?`. An `@expo/vector-icons` set also doesn't type-check as the `IconSet` of `createVectorIconsResolver`.

`@rootnative/core` bundles `@material/material-color-utilities`, so `createMaterialTheme` needs no extra install.

Wrap the root in the provider:
```tsx
import { ThemeProvider } from '@rootnative/core'

export default function App() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider>
      {/* Your app */}
    </ThemeProvider>
  )
}
```

Import components through the subpath exports (preferred, so the bundler can tree-shake the rest):
```tsx
import { Button } from '@rootnative/components/button'
import { Card } from '@rootnative/components/card'
```

Or from the root:
```tsx
import { Button, Card } from '@rootnative/components'
```

## Requirements

- Platforms: iOS, Android, and web through `react-native-web` 0.21 (web also needs `react-dom`). Electron, macOS, Windows, and other React Native hosts are not tested.
- Expo SDK 58 band: `react >=19.3.0 <20.0.0`, `react-native >=0.88.0 <0.89.0` (developed and tested against RN 0.88.0 / React 19.3.0 / Expo SDK 58). One release line supports one SDK band: SDK 58 takes `0.0.0-alpha.29` and later; SDK 57 takes `0.0.0-alpha.16` to `0.0.0-alpha.28` (`npm install @rootnative/components@0.0.0-alpha.28`).
- Required peers (npm and pnpm install them for you; with Yarn classic, add them by hand): `@rootnative/core` (a peer of `@rootnative/components`), `@rootnative/inertia >=0.0.26 <0.1.0` (the animation engine, a peer of both `core` and `components`), `react-native-safe-area-context >=4` (AppBar, BottomAppBar, BottomSheet, Dialog, Layout, NavigationBar, NavigationDrawer, SearchView, SideSheet, Snackbar), `react-native-svg >=15` (CircularProgress, LoadingIndicator). The last two are static imports in the built output, so Metro needs them installed even when you never render the component that uses them.
- Optional peers: `react-native-reanimated >=4.5.0 <4.6.0` and `react-native-worklets >=0.10.0 <0.11.0`, version-locked to each other, so keep both inside these ranges; and `@react-native-vector-icons/material-design-icons >=13`, imported only by the `@rootnative/components/mdi` subpath.
- No package manager installs an *optional* peer for you (npm and pnpm install only the required peers; Yarn classic installs none). `createMaterialTheme` needs no extra install: `@rootnative/core` bundles `@material/material-color-utilities`.

`react-native-reanimated` powers the state-layer transitions and the gesture-driven components (Slider, Switch). Every interactive component needs it. You can skip it only when you use Badge, Divider, Icon, KeyboardAvoidingWrapper, Portal and Typography and nothing else (the only components with no animated value; `Layout` is not on the list because `Grid` animates through `Stagger`). Expo SDK 58 bundles it, and it works in Expo Go.

The components never import `react-native-reanimated` directly. They animate through `@rootnative/inertia`, which resolves the motion tokens of the theme by name and collapses every transition to a hard cut when the OS reduce-motion setting is on. `ThemeProvider` sets this up, so there is nothing to configure. Override it per subtree with `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="always" | "never">` from `@rootnative/inertia`.

Reanimated 4 runs on `react-native-worklets` (installed above). Expo SDK 58 bundles its Babel plugin, so there is nothing to configure. On bare React Native, add `'react-native-worklets/plugin'` as the last entry of the `plugins` in `babel.config.js`.

- Components: https://rootnative.github.io/ui/components/button

## CLI

```bash
npx rootnative create                    # Scaffold a new project (interactive)
npx rootnative create my-app             # Scaffold with name
npx rootnative create my-app -y          # Non-interactive (defaults)
npx rootnative create -t with-router     # Use router template
npx rootnative init                      # Initialize existing project for CLI workflow
npx rootnative add button card           # Copy component source into your project
npx rootnative update                    # Update installed components
npx rootnative upgrade                   # Upgrade @rootnative/core + install new peer deps
npx rootnative list                      # List available components
npx rootnative doctor                    # Check project health
```

Every command that installs packages accepts `--package-manager <pm>` to override the auto-detection (`npm`, `yarn`, `pnpm`, `bun`).

The `create` command is the fastest way to start a new project. The `init` + `add` workflow adds components as source files to an existing project (the copy-paste workflow, like shadcn/ui).

## Full API reference

- [llms-full.txt](https://rootnative.github.io/ui/llms-full.txt): the complete API reference, with all component props, types, and usage examples in one file, written for LLMs.

## Per-package LLM docs

Each published npm package ships its own `llms.txt`, which an AI tool can read from `node_modules`:

- `@rootnative/core` → `node_modules/@rootnative/core/llms.txt` (the theme system API + types)
- `@rootnative/components` → `node_modules/@rootnative/components/llms.txt` (all component props)
- `@rootnative/icons` → `node_modules/@rootnative/icons/llms.txt` (the Lucide / Phosphor / vector-icons adapters)
- `@rootnative/seo` → `node_modules/@rootnative/seo/llms.txt` (the SEO checklist and the head, schema, react, expo-router and node APIs)
- `@rootnative/cli` → `node_modules/@rootnative/cli/llms.txt` (the CLI commands)
